sections.html:
Nelson County taxes real estate at $0.56 per $100 of assessed value. Payment comes in two installments. Spring bills go in the mail May 1 with a June 5 deadline, and fall bills go out October 1 with a December 5 deadline. A countywide reassessment took effect January 1, 2026, so phone the Commissioner's office to check the rate on your own bill before quoting it to a buyer.

Tax or billRate or timing
Real estate$0.56 per $100
Personal property$2.79 per $100
Machinery and tools$1.25 per $100
Spring billMailed May 1, due June 5
Fall billMailed October 1, due December 5

Real estate and personal property tax can be paid online at officialpayments.com using a credit card plus either the bill number or the tax map number. The site adds a convenience fee that scales with the payment. With only two bills a year, a missed December 5 deadline leaves an open balance that a title company will find when it asks for a payoff.

Nelson County splits assessment from collection, as most Virginia localities do. One office decides what your property is worth: the Commissioner of the Revenue. A different one, the Treasurer, mails bills and accepts money. Questions about value go to the Commissioner. Questions about paying or getting a payoff go to the Treasurer.

  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 84 Courthouse Square, P.O. Box 246, Lovingston, VA 22949, phone 434-263-7070.
  • County Administrator, including Board of Equalization scheduling: 84 Courthouse Square, phone 434-263-7000. The Board's appointment line is 434-263-7003.
  • Reassessment office: 800-213-7314, staffed by the appraisal firm the county hired for the project.

Lovingston is the county seat. The Clerk of the Circuit Court's office can tell you about recording fees and forms ahead of closing day.

Nelson County reassessed every property effective January 1, 2026, and the next full reappraisal follows a four year schedule. Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group did the field work with the Commissioner's office. Va. Code 58.1-3252 sets the default at four years, or three if the board votes for it, while a county with 50,000 or fewer residents may stretch the gap to five or six years.

Appraisers visited properties starting in fall 2024. They carried photo IDs, put magnetic signs on their vehicles, and took exterior photos and measurements. Notices of proposed values were expected in November 2025.

Exterior photos say nothing about the rooms inside. If your kitchen is torn out, your roof leaks or a floor is unfinished, ask what the county's record says about your parcel. Fixing the record before you list heads off a dispute with a buyer.

Owners who think a value is out of line with similar properties, or above what the house would sell for, take the case to the Board of Equalization. The board may raise the figure, cut it or affirm it. The county's public notice cites Va. Code 58.1-3378 and 58.1-3379.

  • Where: the Bridge Conference Room of the Lovingston courthouse.
  • Appointments: booked by calling 434-263-7003, scheduled every 30 minutes.
  • Burden: the county's number is presumed correct, so you need a preponderance of evidence showing non-uniformity or a value above the market.

The board sits after a reassessment, not every year. Ring the appointment line to find out if a session is open and when applications close. Collect nearby comparable sales, photos of defects, and any appraisal or contractor estimate you hold. Evidence about your own house beats general complaints about the rate.

Nelson County is rural. The 2020 population was 14,775, and no city or incorporated town sits inside the county lines. Out of 9,871 housing units, 34.5 percent sat vacant in 2020, a sign of the second homes and vacation properties near Wintergreen Resort and Nellysford. Of the homes people live in, 78.7 percent were owner occupied. Listings range from mountain cabins to farm parcels to family houses, and tax and road access questions differ for each.

Creek valleys in the county can fill quickly, and Hurricane Camille caused deadly flash floods here in 1969. If your house is close to a stream, pull together whatever flood or drainage records you have before listing, since buyers will ask. Check the parcel against the county or the FEMA map before you describe its flood status.

Real estate tax outranks every other lien under Va. Code 58.1-3340. At closing, the buyer or a foreclosure trustee pays it out of the proceeds, along with penalty and interest. Once paid, the Treasurer lifts the lien. How the year's tax is split between seller and buyer is a matter of contract, so write down who covers the current half.

Splitting a parcel off a bigger tract changes the math: the tax follows the portion of the price. A low price may lead the Commissioner to request an appraisal. If you sell five acres from a farm, the whole tract's taxes will come up at closing.

A separate grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 comes from Va. Code 58.1-802. Sellers owe it by default, though the parties can agree differently, and the clerk of court takes it when recording the deed.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Lovingston office
sections.html: Come with documents. A bill or tax map number, photo ID, and your deed or settlement statement if you bought lately will answer most questions. For a value dispute, add photographs, repair quotes and prices from comparable sales nearby. Staff can say whether a fix is possible today or must wait for an appeal session. Note the date and who helped you.

Four steps keep tax from stalling a sale. Request a written payoff from the Treasurer, with penalty and interest included. Look at the spring and fall bills to see which is paid. Warn the title company about any parcel split so the tract rule gets applied. Then read the contract's proration line and confirm it matches your plan.

Timing matters on a rural sale. Ask for the payoff early, because a parcel with several tax map numbers may need a separate figure for each. If the buyer is a lender-financed purchaser, the lender will want proof that taxes are current, and the title company usually collects that from the Treasurer. Cleaning up a balance before you list means one fewer item on the closing checklist and a faster path to a signed contract.

When the balance is big or repairs are beyond your budget, an as-is cash sale can pay the tax from proceeds on closing day. You skip repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal, but you still want the payoff letter and a careful look at the settlement statement.

faqs.q: What is the Nelson County property tax rate?
faqs.a: Real estate is taxed at $0.56 per $100. The reassessment that took effect January 1, 2026 may affect your bill, so ask the Commissioner's office what rate applies to you.

faqs.q: When are Nelson County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Two payments: June 5 for the May 1 mailing, and December 5 for the October 1 mailing.

faqs.q: Who handles assessments in Nelson County?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue, at 84 Courthouse Square in Lovingston, phone 434-263-7070.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Nelson County reassessment?
faqs.a: Yes, in front of the Board of Equalization, which meets after a reassessment. Call 434-263-7003 about sessions and appointment times.

faqs.q: Can I sell Nelson County land with taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien is settled from your proceeds, and a partial sale of a tract is prorated by price. Get a payoff from the Treasurer first.
